item.text: {"case_id":"SPR00235","decision":"candidate","candidate_ranking":["C15","C17","C06"],"selected_candidate_label":"C15","confidence":0.78,"relationship_type":"both","rationale":"C15 plausibly supplied a material template for the child’s concluding justification: both reject a private benefits bill because it creates an individual exception to generally applicable benefit rules and violates uniformity and equality of treatment. The child adapts that machinery from veterans’ benefits to civil-service retirement. C17 and C06 contain similar anti-preference reasoning, but C15 has the closest combination of benefits-program context, special-exception framing, and equality language.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"To confer such a preferential advantage on one individual participant in the retirement program would be highly discriminatory","parent_excerpt":"This measure, in providing a special exception from the general laws administered by the Veterans' Administration, would render this claimant potentially eligible to receive a pension","explanation":"Both characterize the private bill as an individualized exception conferring eligibility or benefits unavailable under the governing general program."},{"child_excerpt":"contrary to the principles of fair play and equality of treatment which are basic to sound personnel administration","parent_excerpt":"The Federal programs for veterans and their beneficiaries, if they are to be successful, require unswerving uniformity of rule and equality of treatment to all who are similarly situated.","explanation":"The child closely adapts C15’s equality-of-treatment rationale to civil-service personnel administration."},{"child_excerpt":"The record on H.R. 4546 discloses no valid justification for the favored position the bill would accord this claimant.","parent_excerpt":"I cannot agree that the principles and rules of administration prescribed in the general law should be set aside except in unique and most compelling circumstances of equity.","explanation":"Both require exceptional justification before departing from general benefit-administration rules for a single claimant."}]}
